text: By late September, the Tavrin Valley’s slopes had already turned the color of old parchment, but the mood in the farming hamlets was darker than the season suggested. This year’s crop failure centered on barley, the valley’s most dependable staple and the grain that has filled granaries here since the first irrigation channels were cut in 1987. According to the Tavrin Cooperative’s report released Monday, 1,240 hectares of barley produced less than a third of the five-year average after a cold snap in April and a persistent rust outbreak in June. “We planted on time, we watered on time, and still it came to nothing,” said grower Lenka Moroz, standing beside a half-empty silo near Drevnik. Officials now expect emergency feed imports before winter.
